I couldn't write any notes on Isaiah 33. None of the pages loaded, so I have nothing from the sources to report.

My first attempt to fetch the pages failed because of an error in my own code. The tool then refused any further calls for this turn. I never got to read Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary or Precept Austin. Your rules say to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't drafted anything.

If you ask me to try again in a new message, I'll:

1. **Load the main verse-by-verse sources first:**
   - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-33/
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/isaiah/33.htm
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/isaiah/33.htm
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/isaiah/33.htm
   - Precept Austin's Isaiah 33 page
2. **Search for where the traditions differ.** These are the passages most likely to divide them:
   - who the "destroyer" in v. 1 is (Assyria or Sennacherib, or something more symbolic)
   - who "the King in His beauty" in v. 17 is (Hezekiah, the Messiah or both)
   - the "consuming fire" and the description of the righteous in vv. 14–16
   - forgiveness and healing in v. 24
3. **Look for other views** in NET Bible notes, Bible Odyssey, and Catholic and Orthodox sources (New Advent's Church Fathers, catholic.com, oca.org). I'll also check whether any of the allowed sites discuss v. 24 in connection with healing or prosperity teaching.
4. **Write the notes verse by verse** ("v. 4: ...") with a URL after each point, and leave out any verse I can't find support for.
